companies.name: Translight Solar
companies.text: A retailer selling panels, inverters and batteries from a shop in Accra. Buying here means the panel is already cleared, so the price you see is the price you pay.

companies.name: Deep Solar Ghana
companies.text: Supplies panels for homes and small businesses and handles the installation. Useful if you would rather not arrange a fitter separately.

companies.name: Optima Solar Systems
companies.text: Focuses on larger panels for offices and shops. Stock changes with what has recently cleared the port, so prices move through the year.

companies.name: Led's Go Solar
companies.text: Sits close to Tema port, which keeps inland transport short. Often carries the high wattage bifacial panels used on flat commercial roofs.

companies.name: TALESUN
companies.text: One of the largest solar manufacturers in the world. Its Hi-MO range is widely imported into Ghana, and the base price is low because you are buying at the factory end.
companies.imageAlt: Logo of TALESUN, a Chinese solar panel manufacturer.

companies.name: Jinko Solar
companies.text: Makes the Tiger Neo panels found in the catalogue. Importing directly cuts the retail markup, but you take on shipping, duty and clearing yourself.
companies.imageAlt: Logo of Jinko Solar, a Chinese solar panel manufacturer.

companies.name: Trina Solar
companies.text: Produces the Vertex range, including smaller panels that suit tight roofs. Minimum order sizes usually make direct import worthwhile only for bigger jobs.
companies.imageAlt: Placeholder image for Trina Solar, to be replaced with a photo of their panels

companies.name: JA Solar
companies.text: Supplies the DeepBlue panels in this catalogue. Efficiency is high, which matters when the roof is small and you cannot simply add more panels.
